we have shown that a Bayesian network can be constructed from an arbitrary set of digital forensic evidence items, that this Bayesian network can be used to calculate the evidential weight of each evidence item, that the evidential weights of the evidence items can then be used in a triage scheme, and that this triage scheme is near-optimal in that it maximises the probability of the true perpetrator of the offence being included in the set of suspects that is presented to the court.

the evidential weight of an individual item of evidence is highly dependent on its context.

, when a digital forensic investigation involves multiple sources of evidence, the relative importance of each item of evidence can be quantified using a Bayesian network, and that this information can be used to determine an optimal, cost-effective triaging scheme.
